records.title: Effectively writing low propagation and bend loss waveguides in the silica glass by using a femtosecond laser
records.material: silica glass (grade not stated in abstract)
records.writing_regime: multiscan (label taken from Ackermann et al. 2025 Introduction, not from the abstract); optimal effective writing speed 125 um/s (abstract)
records.waveguide_type: type I / multiscan (inferred)
records.loss_method: not stated in abstract; full text not accessible (Optica page behind Radware captcha, not bypassed)
records.bend_radius_mm_and_loss: 0.001 dB/mm (= 0.01 dB/cm) at bend radius 30 mm (abstract; wavelength not stated)
records.quote: A record low propagation loss of 0.07 dB/cm is achieved
records.notes: The abstract (Crossref-deposited) does NOT state the wavelength. Skryabin et al. 2024 (Sec. I, ref [60]) says 'record low PL of 0.07 dB/cm ... at 1550 nm with a total chip IL of 1.07 dB'; Ackermann et al. 2025 also cites 0.07 dB/cm for Tan et al. without a wavelength. So 1550 nm is a SECONDARY attribution only; wavelength_nm left null on purpose.

records.title: Femtosecond laser writing low-loss waveguides in silica glass: highly symmetrical mode field and mechanism of refractive index change
records.writing_regime: loss depends on pulse repetition rate (abstract); regime not stated in abstract
records.waveguide_type: single-mode type I (inferred)
records.quote: The waveguides exhibit a low propagation loss of 0.15 dB/cm
records.notes: Skryabin et al. 2024 Sec. I cites 0.15 dB/cm 'at the wavelength of 1550 nm [58,59]' (refs = Amorim 2017 and this paper): secondary attribution, wavelength not in the abstract. Mode-field symmetry depends on polarization (abstract).

records.title: Femtosecond-laser-written low-loss multiscan waveguides in fused silica
records.writing_regime: multiscan, 515 nm, 270 fs, 1 MHz, 14-70 nJ, 1 mm/s default
records.waveguide_type: type I multiscan, square-shaped
records.bend_radius_mm_and_loss: additional bend loss 0.1 dB/cm at R=30 mm and 0.026 dB/cm at R=60 mm (Sec. III.4)
records.where_in_text: abstract; Sec. II (920 nm, H-polarization); Sec. III.4 (cut-back, bend loss)
records.quote: Propagation losses in the fabricated waveguides amounted to 0.07 dB/cm.
records.notes: Measured at 920 nm (Toptica CTL950) with horizontal (H) polarization. Coupling loss 0.2 dB/facet average, mode overlap >98.8% with SMF. NOT a 1550 nm measurement; the '1550 nm' remark in Sec. I refers to Tan 2022. Full text read from arXiv v1.

records.title: High-speed femtosecond UV laser writing of low-loss waveguides in fused silica
records.writing_regime: UV low-pulse-density regime: 343 nm (3rd harmonic of Yb laser), 450 fs, 200 kHz, 2-3 pulses/um, 75-225 nJ; 10 mm/s effective speed for a full waveguide
records.waveguide_type: multiscan: 10 adjacent lines at 1 um spacing, single-mode at 1550 nm (index contrast ~0.5e-3)
records.loss_method: cut-back, 13 cm down to 2.5 cm, slope fit of 6-8 points; error from fit uncertainty
records.quote: The lowest propagation loss measured is 0.06 ± 0.02 dB/cm
records.notes: As-written minimum 0.06 +/- 0.02 dB/cm (175 nJ, 2.5 pulses/um, perpendicular writing polarization). After 30 min anneal at 300 C: 0.02 +/- 0.04 dB/cm (225 nJ, 2 pulses/um, parallel polarization), error larger than the value. Abstract: 'below 0.1 dB/cm ... among the lowest values reported for fused silica'. Raw text read from the EPFL Infoscience open-access text layer (CC BY); the Optica page is captcha-blocked. The paper cites Tan 2022 and Skryabin 2024 as 0.07 dB/cm.

records.title: Heat accumulation regime of femtosecond laser writing in fused silica and Nd:phosphate glass
records.writing_regime: heat accumulation regime (inter-pulse time below thermal diffusion time)
records.waveguide_type: tubular depressed-cladding (type III-like)
records.loss_method: not stated in abstract (full text paywalled)
records.quote: We demonstrated low-loss (0.3 dB/cm) tubular waveguide inside fused silica.
records.notes: Abstract also: loss difference between orthogonal polarizations as small as 0.1 dB/cm; induced index change grows from 4e-3 to 6.5e-3 in fused silica. Guiding wavelength is NOT in the abstract, so it cannot be assigned to 1530-1565 nm.

records.title: Low bend loss femtosecond laser written waveguides exploiting integrated microcrack
records.writing_regime: multiscan (repetition rate not extracted)
records.waveguide_type: multiscan 10x10 um waveguide with femtosecond-induced integrated microcrack on the outer bend edge
records.loss_method: not stated in the passages read (straight-waveguide loss quoted as the lower limit of the bend loss)
records.bend_radius_mm_and_loss: 1 dB/cm at R=10 mm at 1550 nm (both polarizations); at 1310 nm 1 dB/cm at R=8.5 mm; at 1550 nm 3 dB/cm at R=6 mm (x-pol) / 8.3 mm (y-pol) (Results, Fig. 5d)
records.where_in_text: abstract (bend loss); Results text (straight loss 0.10 dB/cm at 1.31 um and 0.15 dB/cm at 1.55 um)
records.quote: losses down to 1 dB/cm at 10 mm bend radius were achieved
records.notes: Straight-waveguide propagation loss 0.15 dB/cm at 1.55 um (0.10 at 1.31 um) from the Results text. Authors state the previous lowest was 2.7 dB/cm at the same wavelength and radius. Waveguides re-characterised after 1 year.

records.title: Low bend loss, high index, composite morphology ultra-fast laser written waveguides for photonic integrated circuits
records.venue: Light: Advanced Manufacturing 5, 8 (2024) [Crossref: vol 5 issue 1, art. 52]
records.writing_regime: thermal / cumulative-heating (800 nm, 50 fs, 5.1 MHz) and composite thermal + athermal multi-pass
records.waveguide_type: type I thermal waveguide and composite (thermal + athermal multiscan) waveguide
records.loss_method: composite: segments of 8 to 2 mm, slope of insertion loss ('analogous to a cutback'); thermal: insertion loss of 4 reference waveguides minus coupling loss, divided by length
records.bend_radius_mm_and_loss: 1.0 dB/cm bend-loss cut-off radius: abstract 10 mm -> 4 mm; Results/Discussion 11.0 mm (thermal) -> 3.5 mm (composite)
records.quote: Linear Propagation - Thermal 0.18 dB cm-1
records.notes: Table 1: thermal 0.18 dB/cm, composite 0.50 dB/cm, mode-field mismatch 0.06 dB, athermal termination 0.18 dB. Abstract (4 mm) and Results (3.5 mm) differ slightly. Index contrast 1.12e-2 (composite) vs 6.5e-3 (thermal). Read from arXiv v2 text.

records.title: On-chip beam rotators, adiabatic mode converters, and waveplates through low-loss waveguides with variable cross-sections

records.title: Suppression of bend loss in writing of three-dimensional optical waveguides with femtosecond laser pulses
records.writing_regime: 800 nm, 50 fs, 1 kHz, single scan at 0.03 mm/s with slit-shaped beam
records.waveguide_type: slit-beam waveguide sandwiched between two modification walls (bend-loss suppression walls)
records.loss_method: scattered-light imaging along the straight section at 633 nm (exponential fit)
records.bend_radius_mm_and_loss: R=15 mm (5 deg arc): bend insertion loss reduced from 3~4 dB to ~0.3 dB with walls; measured at 780 nm
records.where_in_text: Conclusions; Results (Figs. 3-5); abstract (>1 order of magnitude at R=15 mm)
records.quote: was reduced from 3~4 dB to ~0.3 dB

records.title: Tailoring the birefringence of femtosecond-laser-written multi-scan waveguides in glass

records.loss_method: not stated; cut-back used for birefringence/phase delay
records.where_in_text: Results, Sec. III.1 (optimization of standard waveguides)
records.quote: which results in 0.33 dB/cm propagation loss
records.notes: Value is for the symmetric inner-to-outer scan order (vertical birefringence axis); coupling loss to SMF 0.13 dB; birefringence b0=(5.5+/-0.2)e-5. Preprint, not peer reviewed; no DOI (arXiv abs page resolved).

records.title: Femtosecond laser additive and subtractive micro-processing: enabling a high-channel-density silica interposer for multicore fibre to silicon-photonic packaging
records.writing_regime: 515 nm, 250 fs, 500 kHz, single scan, optimum 160 nJ
records.waveguide_type: single-scan type I 3D waveguide fanout (nanograting tracks for sockets)
records.loss_method: insertion loss compared for 25.4 mm and 12.7 mm long waveguides (two-length cut-back style), fibre butt coupling
records.bend_radius_mm_and_loss: minimum bend radius 60 mm selected (Sec. 2.2); 'bending loss became appreciable for a 60 mm radius' (Sec. 3.1)

records.title: Laser Structured Optical Interposer for Ultra-Dense Surface Coupling of Multicore Fibers to Silicon Photonic Chip
records.venue: Journal of Lightwave Technology 44(18), 7978-7986 (Sep 2026); arXiv v1 title: 'Laser Structured Optical Interposer for Ultra-dense Vertical Coupling of Multi-core Fibers to Silicon Photonic Chip'
records.material: fused silica wafer, 1 mm (manuscript: 'PG&O, Corning 7980 polished fused silica?')
records.writing_regime: 515 nm (frequency-doubled), ~250 fs, 500 kHz, single continuous scan at 0.1 mm/s, 128-168 nJ depending on depth
records.waveguide_type: single-scan type I 3D waveguides at depths 50-320 um + FLICE TIR micro-mirrors
records.loss_method: insertion loss of 0.5-inch samples minus 0.3 dB coupling loss inferred from mode mismatch (not a cut-back); depth-dependent
records.bend_radius_mm_and_loss: S-bends R=50 mm: 0.5 dB average (100 um horizontal offset), 0.4 dB average (50 um vertical offset)
records.network_description: 3D interposer: 40 channels from 6 multicore fibres onto a 2D grid of Si grating couplers; Design C uses many waveguide-waveguide intersections
records.where_in_text: arXiv v1 Section II (design) and Section IV text + Table I ('Additional intersect loss (100 deg) < 0.01 dB/intersect')
records.quote: yielding at most 0.01 dB per intersect
records.notes: CROSSING DATA POINT. Crossing angle 80 deg (text) = 100 deg (Table I); up to 16 crossings in series showed no significant additional loss, <=0.01 dB per intersect (an upper bound). Crosstalk: 'no measurable crosstalk above the 40 dB noise floor' => crossing_crosstalk_db=-40 is a BOUND (crosstalk below -40 dB), not a measurement. Propagation loss 0.20 dB/cm is at 50 um depth (0.56/0.65/0.71 dB/cm at 140/230/320 um). Numbers read from arXiv v1 (manuscript still has template placeholders and a '?' on the glass grade); the published JLT version was not opened.

not_found: Per-crossing insertion loss of fs-written waveguide crossings in glass: only ONE verified data point (Djogo/Rahimnouri/Herman, fused silica, 1550 nm: <=0.01 dB per intersect at 80/100 deg, up to 16 crossings; crosstalk below the -40 dB noise floor). No second independent measurement found; no data for 90 deg or small crossing angles; no peer-reviewed loss/crosstalk for fs-glass 'X-junction' or 'overpass' structures; no per-crossing number in Peri 2026, Martin 2023 (3D beam combiner), Kondratyev 2024, Pentangelo 2024, Hoch 2022 or Cao 2026 although several rely on 3D crossovers or avoid planar crossings.

Verified Tan et al. 2022 measurement wavelength: the abstract has none; Optica page and PDF are blocked by captcha (not bypassed). 1550 nm only via Skryabin et al. 2024 Sec. I. Tan 2021 (0.15 dB/cm) likewise.

Lowest verified depressed-cladding (type III) loss at 1530-1565 nm in any glass: NOT established. Candidates lack either the wavelength (Bukharin 2015: 0.3 dB/cm fused silica; Likhov 2025 K8: 0.8 dB/cm 'telecom range') or the number (Zhou 2025 SK1310, Wu 2025 ULE glass-ceramic, Liao 2016 ZBLAN). A search-engine excerpt mentioned 0.9 dB/cm at 1600 nm for a depressed-cladding guide in tellurite glass (Smayev/Okhrimchuk) but the abstract could not be opened, so it is NOT recorded.
Full texts blocked by captcha/403 and not bypassed: Optica (OL, OE, OME), ScienceDirect (Zhou 2025, Smayev 2018), Wiley (Yu 2026), MDPI HTML (Lichtenegger 2026), SPIE/IOP raw HTML, IEEE.
Propagation-loss figure inside Cao 2026 (LAMP): none in the main text (may be in the Supplementary Information, not opened).

fs-written 3D photonic neural network in glass after 2024: only Cao et al. 2026 (LAMP) found. Optoelectron. 19(2), 20, 2026, doi 10.2738/foe.2026.0020, Crossref-verified) exists but its abstract/text could not be retrieved.
